global_human_reading.first_question: What practical task does the player face, what does the chosen move accomplish or miss, and what response/cost changes that judgment?
claim_levels: Exact legal option and actor identity
Usefulness against an adequate current opponent response
Cause and robustness of the original root numerical assessment
global_human_reading.separation: A proven earlier level never automatically satisfies the next. A changed actor or optional path event is not failure if the necessary function remains valid; a legal route is not useful merely because it survives.
global_human_reading.minimum_purpose: A quiet improvement or one of several good plans may need only the concrete useful purpose plus any consequential immediate cost. Do not require a long invented contrast for every ordinary move.
global_human_reading.mistake_and_sacrifice: A serious mistake or sacrifice needs the consequential counter and compensation/cost. Evaluate practical resistance separately from objective forced loss.
global_human_reading.counter_priority: Inspect the source strongest or most resilient named opponent reply before treating a pleasing cooperative tactical line as the answer; a numerical or all-major-defense claim requires a separate owned unrestricted comparison.
global_human_reading.withdrawal: Retain explanations by minimal functional prerequisites, including adequate defender/price, not by a broad ordered event list. Conversely, do not retain a useful/root-winning claim after an adequate counter changes its required value.
global_human_reading.generalization: Success requires the selected basic answer to recover the actual move judgment, needed response and price under these fixed criteria. Shorter text, more facts, longer calculation, or matching an author’s PV alone does not count.

scenes.human_question: How should Black improve the underemployed e7 knight without prematurely surrendering the useful c4 knight or b6 pawn, and why can the same c4–d6 move become useful later?

source_judgment.root_Ng8: Author-preferred improvement: reroute Ne7 through g8/f6, restoring d5 support and retaining e4/g4 possibilities.
source_judgment.root_Nd6: Author criticizes the immediate Nc4–d6; Rxb6 followed by a5 makes White’s extra a-pawn important.
source_judgment.late_Nd6: After the source Ng8–Nf6 maneuver and White Ng3, the author prefers Nd6 to a premature Nf6–e4. This preserves the choice of which knight later reaches e4.
source_judgment.alternatives: Ng6 is a viable but awkward alternative because the bishop on h4 can occupy the knight’s intended square. Kh7/rook moves and g5 are also source-discussed choices, so author preference does not imply every other move loses.

minimum_basic_comments.root_Ng8: Improve the least active knight via g8 and f6. On f6 it supports d5 and keeps central or kingside options; Black need not rush the well-placed c4 knight away.
minimum_basic_comments.root_Nd6: This commits the c4 knight too soon and permits Rxb6. In the book reply Black cannot recover that pawn cheaply, and White’s extra a-pawn becomes useful.
minimum_basic_comments.late_Nd6: Now Nd6 keeps the choice of which knight to exchange on e4. In the book’s e4 exchanges, the surviving f6 knight is ready for d5; the original e7 knight does not have to be the one that enters e4.
minimum_basic_comments.late_Ne4: Immediate Nf6–e4 commits to an exchange too soon. The book explains that the resulting structure reduces the pressure on e3; Nd6 keeps more useful choices.

scenes.basic_purpose_sufficient_scope: A root Ng8 purpose explanation can be a complete ordinary-move answer if it names the improvement and d5 support and does not invent a unique numerical reason. It need not print the whole later attack. A claim that Nd6 is inferior or that Ng8 is uniquely best requires the corresponding comparison and consequential reply.
minimum_functional_conditions: The identified underemployed original Nb8 is at e7 and can legally use the g8–f6 route; it is different from the original Ng8 already established on c4.

The temporary reduction of d5 support must not allow an adequate immediate White counter before Nf6 restores support. The book assesses White as too passive; legal geometry alone does not prove this adequacy judgment.
If the c4 knight moves to d6, the b6 pawn’s capture and recapture context must be checked at that exact decision time. The same legal move and same legal ...Rc6xb6 do not imply the same cost.
After White Ng3, e4 exchange timing and the identity of the surviving knight matter. Keep the available functions, rather than requiring one original knight to perform every named later action.
The h4 destination cannot serve two friendly pieces at once. Ng6–h4 is legal in abstract but becomes unavailable while the chosen bishop is retained on h4.
optional_events_not_required: The root e7 knight itself reaching e4. The author-preferred late Nd6 route can instead send the c4 knight to e4 while the first knight remains on f6 ready for d5.
White choosing exactly Rf1/Be1/Ng3, then Qb1 or Reb1. These are source example realizations, not proof that all original root defenses force the same course.
The later game Qe1 blunder, exact Ng4 mating attack or eventual result. Those cannot be imported as the cause of the original quiet move.

price_and_legality.matched_action: Early and late Black Nc4–d6 is c4d6 by black_N_g8. It is legal in both.
price_and_legality.early_context: After early Nd6 Rxb6, Black Rc6xb6 is legal, but White Rb1xb6 is also legal. The queen cannot immediately recapture on b6 because the new Nd6 blocks its path from e6. Black’s rook recapture therefore does not cheaply refute White’s pawn capture.
price_and_legality.late_context: After Ng8 Rf1 Bh4 Be1 Bxe1 Rxe1 Nf6 Ng3 Nd6 Rxb6, the same Black Rc6xb6 is legal. All immediate legal White captures of that rook were enumerated; none exist. The original White Rh1 is now on e1 rather than b1.
price_and_legality.important_boundary: These local capture ledgers explain a changed price constraint. They do not by themselves prove that late Nd6 beats every alternative or that the original Ng8 numerical evaluation is caused exclusively by the rook relocation.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: 37.Rxb6, then ...Ne4 38.a5; or inspect the apparently natural ...Rxb6 and its complete immediate recapture inventory.
required_counter_checks.scope: Source and exact local legality, not an unrestricted best-reply proof.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: 41.Qb1 is the more resilient author reply; 41.Reb1 permits a tactical sequence. Also compare actual 40...Ne4 41.Nxe4 dxe4.
required_counter_checks.scope: The Qb1 and Reb1 examples cannot establish every White response or a unique best knight route.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: White’s most effective attempts to exploit d5 or obtain active pieces during the g8–f6 route; compare Ng6 Rf1 Bh4 Rfb1.
required_counter_checks.scope: An eventual product usefulness/root-ranking claim requires an owned complete opponent search, not just the book’s selected variation.

falsifiers_and_misleading_comments: Wrong: Ng8 creates the legal possibility of Nd6. The same c4d6 move was already legal.
Wrong: the original e7 knight must later reach e4 or the Ng8 idea has failed. Another original knight can supply that event while the first supplies d5/g4 functions.
Wrong: Black can still capture the rook on b6, therefore early and late positions have the same value. Their immediate legal recaptures differ.
Wrong: Nc4–d6 is always bad because the root book move was criticized; the later exact source position explicitly recommends it.
Wrong: Ng8 uniquely causes the eventual mating attack. The author gives multiple routes and later independent errors.
Withdraw or narrow the improvement/safety claim if an adequate current defense exploits d5 before support returns, even if the old route remains legal.
scenes.unresolved: The relative root numerical ranking and robustness against every major White response have not been computed in this reading. The derived b6 price change is not asserted to be the whole root causal explanation.

root.history_scope: The book supplies a diagram without a preceding full game score. Identity starts at this exact diagram FEN; halfmove/fullmove counters are normalized to 0/1 and no unavailable earlier history is invented.

scenes.human_question: How can Black convert a strong passed-pawn clamp into a practical invasion plan while keeping e2 controlled, even when the defender or the selected conversion route changes?

source_judgment.Rd3: Most direct human plan: pressure c3 and transfer toward d2/b2 to restrict Bb3.
source_judgment.Bd3: A strong alternative: reinforce e2 and prepare a rook transfer to f1.
source_judgment.g4: A strong alternative: gain space and improve the king, with further e2 protection before rook invasion.
source_judgment.Be4: Achieves little after Kg1; Black must choose another plan. This is not automatically a lost winning position.
source_judgment.plurality: The author explicitly gives many good moves. A preferred human plan is not a proof that the other sound plans are numerically inferior or mistakes.

minimum_basic_comments.Rd3: Activate the e3 rook against c3 and prepare Rd2 to squeeze the bishop. The passed pawn on e2 remains protected by the other rook as the first one leaves the e-file.
minimum_basic_comments.Bd3: Reinforce the advanced pawn and keep White tied down while preparing a rook on the f-file. That rook move was already legal; the added support matters to the continuing conversion.
minimum_basic_comments.g4: Gain space and give the king g5, while retaining the passed-pawn clamp and preparing more support before rook infiltration.
minimum_basic_comments.Be4: This does not yet advance a useful conversion plan after Kg1; a different arrangement is still needed. Do not exaggerate it into a forced loss.

scenes.basic_purpose_sufficient_scope: The concrete Rd3 purpose can stand as a complete useful basic answer in a position with several strong moves. A long comparison is unnecessary unless the output asserts unique ranking, immediate c3 victory, a forced bishop trap or a particular full numerical cause.
minimum_functional_conditions: The original e2 pawn remains a costly obstruction to White and has an adequate current defender at the time a rook is repurposed. Retaining the original Re3 defender is not required.
After Re3–d3 the e-file is clear and the other original rook Re8 protects e2. Verify this transfer with the same White Re1xe2 attempt, not merely an attack count.
To claim the c3 pawn is won, check White Rc1xc3 and any other immediate legal recapture after ...Rxc3. One rook attacking c3 is not enough to establish a free capture.

In the alternative ...Ree3 route the second rook can supply a different capture/support mechanism, while the ...Rd2 route shifts the pressure toward Bb3. These are separate realizations of conversion.

The Bd3 support plan and king movement must retain the passed-pawn constraint while rooks change files; Rf8 legality alone is not its value. Black Kf6 initially blocks the f-file and later king relocation opens a checking line.
optional_events_not_required: Keeping Re3 on e3 as the permanent pawn defender; after Rd3 the defender is Re8, and later Rd2/Bd3 can supply different support.
White choosing Ra1/Ba2 and the exact Rd2–b2 bishop squeeze. The author also gives a rook liquidation into a winning pawn ending.
The pawn on e2 remaining forever. In the source liquidation it is exchanged as Black reaches a favorable king-and-pawn conversion.
A mating finish rather than an ending, or every good root choice following the same route.

price_and_legality.same_white_attempt: White Re1xe2 is a legal capture in the local analysis before and after ...Rd3. Before the move Re3xe2 answers it; afterwards Re8xe2 does. There are zero immediate legal White recaptures in both checked positions.
price_and_legality.already_available_transfer: Re8–f8 is already legal at the root. Bd3 is therefore not an enabling-legality explanation; it adds functional support and flexibility during the continuing plan.
price_and_legality.important_negative: After Rd3 Kg1, ...Rxc3 is legal but White Rc1xc3 is also legal. The minimal factual comment cannot say Black wins c3 immediately.
price_and_legality.multiple_defenders: After Bd3 and the attempted Re1xe2, both Bd3xe2 and Re3xe2 are legal immediate captures. Do not name one original defender as mandatory.
price_and_legality.scope: Capture and immediate recapture inventories are complete at the named positions. No full optimal conversion or numerical root ranking is established by them.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: The immediate Re1xe2 attempt with every current legal black capturer and every immediate legal White recapture.
required_counter_checks.scope: Necessary factual price check; not proof that White’s strongest overall defense is that capture.

required_counter_checks.purpose: Pressure c3 versus a free win
required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: After ...Rd3 Kg1, inspect ...Rxc3 Rc1xc3. After ...Ree3, inspect the changed support and legal Rc1 route.
required_counter_checks.scope: A complete relevant recapture inventory prevents overstating an attack as a won pawn.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: White Kg1/Kf2, Bc2/Bb1, Ra3 and pawn resistance; compare the Rd2 restriction route and Ree3 liquidation route.
required_counter_checks.scope: Book-named resistance is not an unrestricted best-reply result. Original root numerical judgment still needs a separate owned survey.

falsifiers_and_misleading_comments: Wrong: Re3 leaves e3, so e2 is now undefended. The other original rook now sees e2 down the open e-file.
Wrong: Bd3 makes Rf8 legal. That transfer was already legal.
Wrong: ...Rd3 immediately wins c3. White can legally recapture the lone invading rook in the checked Kg1 position.
Wrong: a different rook supports e2, therefore the original plan has failed. The relevant requirement is adequate pawn constraint, not permanent guard identity.
Wrong: the plan fails if White’s e2 capture or a liquidation removes the passed pawn. A favorable conversion may fulfill the purpose differently.
Wrong: Bd3/g4 are bad because Rd3 is the author’s human preference, or several winning choices need no concrete purpose explanation.
Narrow or withdraw the clamp/invasion claim if a changed defender cannot adequately answer a current capture, forced check or exchange price.
scenes.unresolved: No unrestricted engine response survey was performed. Multiple source-good plans are recognized without assigning a new best score or claiming that pawn protection alone proves the whole conversion.

scenes.human_question: Why is capturing the offered rook with Qxd7 the wrong response, and how does Bxf4 answer the apparent discovered-check queen win without falsely claiming that every White reply loses in that one forced line?

source_judgment.Bxf4: The author’s missed refutation of White’s preceding Rxd7; it takes Nf4 and answers the tempting Rc7+ with Bd7.
source_judgment.Qxd7: The actual error: after Qxe5 and castling White’s pawns, active bishop and safer king outweigh Black’s nominal exchange advantage.
source_judgment.White_Rxb7: The best source-named fighting chance, better than the superficially attractive Rc7+. Accurate ...Bd7 and later ...Rab8 are required; Black should still prevail, but White can resist.
source_judgment.White_Rd4: Another practical defense, with queen exchange and pawn compensation; not the same immediate mating story.

minimum_basic_comments.Bxf4: First take the knight and be ready to meet Rc7+ with Bd7. The apparent queen win then leaves White facing a queen attack and back-rank mating threat. White can instead fight with Rxb7+ or Rd4+, so the one tactical line is not a forced response to every defense.
minimum_basic_comments.Qxd7: Taking the rook allows Qxe5 and White can castle safely. White’s active bishop, safer king and pawn compensation matter more here than the exchange count; Bxf4 was the stronger defensive resource.
minimum_basic_comments.relative_pin: The g3 pawn can legally capture Bf4, but vacating the g-file exposes Bg2 to ...Rxg2. This is a price/constraint, not an absolute legal prohibition.

scenes.basic_purpose_sufficient_scope: A serious mistake needs the missed defensive resource and resulting compensation, not merely the fact that a queen captures a rook. A compact Bxf4 refutation can explain the missed tactic, but a claim of forced mate or an effortless win must also survive Rxb7+/Rd4+ and the accurate black defenses.
minimum_functional_conditions: The original bishop from f8 reaches f4 after taking the original white Ng1 on f4.
After the apparent Rc7+ queen grab, ...Bd7 must be an adequate legal interposition and ...Rxc8 must leave the stated queen attack/back-rank problem.
The bishop’s e5 and d2 control matters in that exact tactical realization; do not treat the whole later source event list as a requirement under a different adequate defense.
The g3 pawn is relatively constrained by exposing Bg2 to Rg8, not absolutely pinned to the king. Legal gxf4 must be retained and its cost checked.

Against White’s stronger Rxb7+ defense, ...Kf8 permits an immediate drawing check cycle and ...Rae8 later dissipates the advantage; a claim of robust advantage must use adequate current defense, including the source ...Bd7/...Rab8 route.
If evaluating actual Qxd7, include White’s safe castling, active bishop and the source pawn recovery. Nominal rook-versus-bishop or exchange price alone does not decide usefulness.
optional_events_not_required: White choosing the faulty Rc7+ queen grab. The stronger source Rxb7+ or Rd4+ answers alter the realization and the kind of advantage.
The original Bf4 staying on f4 forever. In the fighting Rxb7+ line it can be surrendered while Black gains active rooks and a passed a-pawn.
A forced mate in every source-good defense, or the exact final game win after the opponent’s actual Qxd7 error.

price_and_legality.relative_pin: At the Bxf4 position g3xf4 is legal, and Black Rg8xBg2 is a legal capture with no immediate legal White recapture at that checked position. The same is true after the longer queen-liquidation line. The book word “pin” must not be rendered as illegal gxf4.
price_and_legality.nominal_price_warning: Actual ...Qxd7 wins a rook but yields major compensation. The later source legal line leaves White three pawns for the exchange with better king safety and an active bishop; that is a positional/tactical value judgment, not a sufficient raw material formula.
price_and_legality.counter_defense_warning: Rxb7+ Kf8 Qb4+ Kg7 Qd4+ Kf8 gives White a repeatable source check cycle. The source adequate defense is ...Bd7, not the convenient inferior king move.
price_and_legality.scope: These exact legality and immediate-cost facts are complete at their named positions. Overall best defense and numerical root cause are not computed here.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: Rc7+ Bd7 Rxc8+ Rxc8, including queen attack, back-rank threat and Bf4 control.
required_counter_checks.scope: Explains the faulty White idea, not all defenses.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: Rxb7+ with ...Bd7; distinguish the drawing ...Kf8 check cycle and later inadequate ...Rae8 from adequate ...Rab8.
required_counter_checks.scope: Source-best practical defense; no independent full legal-search best-reply certification.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: Rd4+ Qc6, queen exchange and active black endgame pieces.
required_counter_checks.scope: The advantage can become an ending rather than preserving the first mating net.

required_counter_checks.named_source_reply: Qxd7 Qxe5 O-O-O O-O, and subsequent source pawn recovery.
required_counter_checks.scope: Do not infer that every rook capture is a blunder or that three pawns always outweigh an exchange.

falsifiers_and_misleading_comments: Wrong: Bxf4 forces Rc7+ and mate. Stronger legal White fighting replies exist.
Wrong: gxf4 is illegal because the pawn is pinned. The exact board allows it but exposes the other bishop.
Wrong: Qxd7 is good because Black won a rook, or all nominal R-for-N/B costs have the same utility.
Wrong: ...Kf8 after Rxb7+ validates Black’s winning plan. The source demonstrates White’s drawing checks.
Wrong: the tactical idea is invalid merely because the Bf4 actor is later taken; the stronger defense can convert into rook activity and a passed pawn.
Narrow or withdraw a winning claim when a current adequate opponent defense changes the result, even if the initial tactical threat and its example line remain legal.
scenes.unresolved: No engine score, full forced-win proof or strongest unrestricted reply has been obtained. The source distinguishes technical winning chances from practical resistance; criteria retain that boundary.
